summary.name: North Pole Security Workshop and Santa
summary.one_liner: Workshop is a commercial endpoint protection platform for macOS that manages Santa, the open-source allowlisting agent originally created at Google.
use_cases: Block unknown or unapproved software from running on Macs
Stop infostealers from reading browser cookies, credentials and SSH keys
Block USB, SD card and Thunderbolt data exfiltration
Manage software approval requests across a macOS fleet
Feed macOS security telemetry into an existing SIEM
summary.what_it_does: Santa is an open-source macOS security agent that controls which binaries can execute and which apps can access sensitive files, and blocks removable media. Workshop is a centralized console built on Santa for security teams to set policies, define per-team approval workflows (self-service, designated approvers, multi-approver, community voting), and automate allowlisting through Package Rules for Homebrew, npm and GitHub Releases. Workshop includes a customizable risk engine with threat intel integrations such as VirusTotal and ReversingLabs, and custom webhook plugins. Santa and Workshop record telemetry and an audit trail of decisions and actions. The page says organizations can start in Monitor mode and move to Lockdown mode.
notable: Santa is open source and originally created at Google; Workshop is the management layer built on it
Prevention-first: unknown binaries are blocked before they run rather than detected after execution
Per-team approval workflows with delegation, multi-approver and community voting
Santa File Access Authorization to stop infostealers reading sensitive files
caveats: Pricing is not stated on the page; Workshop appears to be a commercial enterprise product
Page says Santa uses well under 0.5% CPU and under 150 MB RAM on a typical fleet, which is a vendor claim
